motion_provenance.what: seated on an upright bench, back on the pad; dumbbells to each side of the shoulders with elbows below the wrists; press up until the arms are extended overhead (compared with the ExRx photo, 14/11)
motion_provenance.source: ExRx 'Dumbbell Shoulder Press' (instructions and photo); free-exercise-db 'Dumbbell Shoulder Press' (Unlicense, used by the app library)

motion_provenance.what: shoulder girdle rhythm (shoulder blade turns ~1 deg per 2 deg of arm elevation past ~30 deg; clavicle elevation)
motion_provenance.source: Inman et al. 1944, J Bone Joint Surg 26(1); McClure et al. 2001, J Shoulder Elbow Surg 10(3)

motion_provenance.what: muscles: anterior and lateral deltoid; triceps and trapezius synergists; serratus anterior turns the shoulder blade up

bench back pad at 70 deg (one notch below vertical, not 90); elbows tucked about 30-45 deg in front of the body (scapular plane); deep bottom with the dumbbells close to the shoulders; palms turned slightly in; shoulders held down (15/11, Kiệt's notes, then checked on video and by search)

start_position: Set the bench back upright (80-85°), sit with your back and head against the pad, feet flat
Dumbbells beside the shoulders, palms forward, elbows under the wrists
concentric: Press straight up over the shoulders
Forearms stay vertical under the weights
top_hold: Arms almost straight above the shoulders; do not bang the weights together
eccentric: Lower slowly back beside the shoulders

validation_profile.comment: Thresholds for automated checks. They catch defects in the animation data (jumps, slides, penetration, asymmetry). They do not certify exercise technique; that needs a qualified human.
validation_profile.max_hand_into_bar_comment: The skin of the palm is rigid in this rig. Up to 8 mm of palm pad inside the bar stands for soft tissue pressed flat by the load; more than that, or any finger passing through the bar, is a defect.

technical_cues: Bench back at 70 deg, back stays on the pad
Shoulders down, elbows tucked a little forward
Lower until the dumbbells nearly touch the shoulders
Elbows under the wrists, press straight up
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back off the pad
Letting the elbows drift behind the body or in front of the face
Bringing the dumbbells together in a V and knocking them at the top
muscle_roles_note: Target anterior deltoid; synergists lateral deltoid, triceps, middle/lower trapezius, serratus anterior (supraspinatus and coracobrachialis are hidden; the clavicular pectoral is left out because the atlas has one pectoral group); biceps is a dynamic stabilizer; upper trapezius stabilizes. Checked against ExRx 15/11 (Kiệt: "nhóm cơ hoạt động đã chính xác chưa").
